links.comparator_used: Radiologist double reading without AI support (historical matched control cohort from the year before AI implementation)
links.outcome: Cancer detection rate and positive predictive value of recalls in population-based screening (DM and DBT combined)
links.effect: CDR 9.0 vs 5.8 per 1000 (+3.2, p<0.001); PPV 14.6% vs 10.6% (+4%, p<0.001); recall rate 6.1% vs 5.4% (+0.7%, p<0.001). For DM alone, the CDR, recall rate and PPV differences were not significant (p=0.055, 0.373, 0.25).
links.tradeoff: Recall rate rose slightly (+0.7%), described as acceptable. Interval cancers and false negatives were not yet known. Single site, one AI system, historical control group.
links.quote: The implementation of an AI system for concurrent decision support for reading DM and DBT screening exams increased the breast cancer detection rate (CDR) by 3.2‰ (9.0‰ vs 5.8‰; p < 0.001) and the positive predictive value (PPV) of the recalled women by 4% (14.6% vs 10.6%; p < 0.001) with an acceptable increase in recall rate (RR) by 0.7% (6.1% vs 5.4%; p < 0.001).

design_hint: concurrent AI decision support for human double reading
